questions.question: Why does the system retrieve candidates before applying a heavy ranker?
options: A heavy model cannot score the full eligible universe within the feed latency budget
Retrieval makes every candidate equally relevant
The ranking stage no longer needs eligibility checks
Candidate retrieval guarantees a perfectly fair slate
questions.explanation: Cheap recall narrows a large eligible set so the service can spend richer feature and model work on a manageable group.

questions.question: At 900K feed opens per second and a 72% reusable-candidate rate, how many requests per second need fresh retrieval, ranking, and policy work?
options: 72K/s
questions.explanation: The fresh path receives the 28% miss share: 900K multiplied by 0.28 equals 252K requests per second.

questions.question: Which decision belongs to the final slate policy rather than an individual ranking score?
options: Preventing one creator from occupying too many positions
Storing the post body
Training an embedding offline
Allocating a database partition
questions.explanation: Creator concentration is visible only when composing the ordered set, so it requires a slate-level constraint.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a ranker misses its deadline?
options: Use a bounded-age eligible fallback and re-run final policy checks
Extend the request until the heavy model returns
Return cached items without policy validation
Expose every followed post chronologically
questions.explanation: A declared fallback can protect latency, but eligibility, safety, and repetition constraints still apply before release.

questions.question: Why should an exposure log include candidate source, model version, and policy version separately?
options: They reveal whether an issue began in recall, prediction, or final constraints
They eliminate the need for privacy controls
They make every experiment statistically valid
They allow raw user data to be retained forever
questions.explanation: Separate versions make a decision diagnosable and replayable while privacy-bounded logging and retention rules remain necessary.

questions.question: What trade-off does hybrid fanout address?
options: It precomputes ordinary social updates while reading high-fanout authors or recommendations on demand
It removes all read-time ranking
It replaces trust and safety with cache invalidation
It guarantees every post is shown to every follower
questions.explanation: Hybrid fanout controls celebrity write amplification without making every feed request depend on fully on-demand graph retrieval.
